The AI Act handles contrary-to-duty obligations (CTDs) involving temporality by stating that certain properties used to be fulfilled but no longer are. An example provided in the document illustrates that if a notifying authority concludes that a notified body no longer meets the requirements, it must investigate the matter. This situation is reformulated to show that the obligation to investigate arises only if the notified body no longer fulfills the requirements, indicating a temporal aspect.

To represent such cases, the suggested logic is Dyadic Deontic Logic (DDL), which allows for the expression of CTDs that arise when ideal obligations have been violated. DDL differentiates between ideal and actual obligations and introduces a conditional obligation operator, making it suitable for representing these scenarios.
